newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO not pressing Israel on detentions-rights group.
newsitem.headline: PLO not pressing Israel on detentions-rights group.

text.p: An Israeli human rights group on Wednesday accused the Palestinian Authority of doing little to obtain the release of Palestinians detained by Israel without trial who were opposed to the peace process.
"Because these are opponents of the Oslo process, they have not done all they could do to get them released," Jessica Montell, of Israel's B'Tselem human rights group, told a news conference.
She did not present evidence for the claim that the detainees opposed the peace process.

Montell made the comment while presenting a B'Tselem report entitled "Prisoners of Peace" on Israel's continuing the practise of detaining Palestinians without trial despite a 1993 interim peace deal with the PLO, hammered out at Oslo.
B'Tselem said Israel currently held 249 Palestinians in "administrative detention" and about 40 percent of them had been detained for more than a year.
The Palestinian Authority official in charge of negotiating with Israel on prisoner releases, Hisham Abd al-Razek, rejected Montell's charge, telling Reuters it was "nonsense".
"The Palestinian Authority does not differentiate between political prisoners. They are all Palestinians, although the majority is pro-Palestinian Authority," Razek said.
Razek said in any event peacemaking was at an impasse and there was currently no opportunity to work to free prisoners.

Peacemaking between Israel and the Palestinians plunged into crisis in March when Israel began building a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem that Palestinians say is aimed at pre-empting final peace talks.

Over the six years of the Palestinian uprising against Israel's occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which ended with the landmark peace accord, Israel detained thousands of Palestinians for varying periods of time without trial.

The group said Israel's use of administrative detention did not meet the stringent requirements of international law because detainees were not told why they were held, how long they would be detained, and the information justifying their detention was often classified.

The Israeli army says administrative detentions can be imposed for up to six months. But the period of detention is renewable, so that some Palestinians find themselves held for years without charge or trial.

"Whenever the period of supposed release comes, we wait and he waits and all of us have dreams about what we're going to do when he comes home, and suddenly the dream disappears," Dr. Rim Zagha, whose husband, Ribhi Qattamesh, has been held for more than three years, told the news conference.
"If they believe he's a danger or he's a terrorist, they must charge him and send him to trial. Otherwise, they must release him," Zagha said.
